At the Monaco Grand Prix, the Stewards imposed a 5 second time penalty and 2 penalty points (total of 2 for the 12 month period). At the Qatar Grand Prix, the Stewards determined that no further action was taken, based on the incident being considered as a typical 'Lap 1, Turn 1' incident. Therefore, the penalties were different for these incidents, even though they cited the same Article in Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2(d).

citations.quote_or_paraphrase: The Stewards reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, timing, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence. Hulkenberg caused a collision on the inside of Turn 6 on the first lap. The Stewards considered that as he dove in and was unable to control the car and was not forced there by any other car this does not get the benefit of the doubt of a first lap incident. Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and Chapter 4 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

Whilst the argument can be made that Car 44 was predominantly at fault, the Stewards, taking into account that the incident happened in Lap 1 and several cars were involved, determine that the incident is considered as a typical ‘Lap 1, Turn 1’ incident and no driver is wholly at fault. Therefore no further action is taken.
